statement: Express $\\sin x+\\sqrt{3}\\cos x$ in the form $R\\sin(x+\\alpha)$ with $R>0$ and $0<\\alpha<\\pi/2$. Hence solve $\\sin x+\\sqrt{3}\\cos x=1$ for $0\\le x<2\\pi$.
solution: $R=\\sqrt{1+3}=2$ and we need $\\cos\\alpha=\\tfrac12$, $\\sin\\alpha=\\tfrac{\\sqrt3}{2}$, so $\\alpha=\\pi/3$. The expression is $2\\sin(x+\\pi/3)$. The equation becomes $2\\sin(x+\\pi/3)=1$, so $\\sin(x+\\pi/3)=\\tfrac12$. Thus $x+\\pi/3=\\pi/6$ or $5\\pi/6$ (mod $2\\pi$), giving $x=-\\pi/6$ or $x=\\pi/2$. In $[0,2\\pi)$ the solutions are $x=\\pi/2$ and $x=11\\pi/6$.
hints: Find R as the square root of the sum of squares.
Identify alpha from cos alpha and sin alpha.
Solve the resulting single sine equation.
